instruction: In the container, the Go repository at /gin (gin-gonic/gin) is checked out. Report the exact full output of the test run (including any compile errors or failures with full messages), and the git info. Do not modify any file. Just report raw output.

Run these and report raw output: `cd /gin && git log --oneline -10`, `cd /gin && git status --porcelain`, `cd /gin && git diff HEAD --stat`, `cd /gin && git log -1 --format='%H %s %ad'`, and `cd /gin && ls -la`. Go repo at /gin (gin-gonic/gin). A bug was injected into /gin/errors.go. A hidden test named TestErrorUnwrap (not present in the repo; the repo's errors_test.go has a similar test that currently passes) must pass after the fix. The hidden version most likely exercises errors.Is / errors.As / errors.Unwrap with a gin.Error **value** (not only *Error), e.g. fmt.Errorf("wrapped: %w", Error{Err: innerErr, Type: ErrorTypeAny}), or asserts `var _ interface{ Unwrap() error } = Error{}`. Investigate /gin/errors.go and /gin/errors_test.go. Write a TEMPORARY probe test file /gin/zz_probe_errors_test.go (you MUST delete it when done) that checks: (a) errors.Is(fmt.Errorf("w: %w", &Error{Err: innerErr}), innerErr) and errors.As with a custom error type; (b) the same with a value Error{...}; (c) errors.Unwrap(&Error{...}) and errors.Unwrap(Error{...}); (d) `var _ interface{ Unwrap() error } = Error{}` and `= &Error{}`. Run `cd /gin && go test -run 'TestErrorUnwrap|Probe' -v ./`. Then make the minimal fix in errors.go so all of these work (most likely: change the Unwrap receiver from pointer to value, i.e. `func (msg Error) Unwrap() error { return msg.Err }`), while keeping the whole suite green: run `cd /gin && go test ./...` before and after. NOTE: other agents are editing other files in this repo concurrently; if a compile error comes from a zz_probe_*_test.go file that is not yours, wait 20s and retry, and never modify files you did not create. Report: exact diff, before/after test results, and confirmation the probe file was deleted.

Go repo at /gin (gin-gonic/gin). TWO bugs were injected into /gin/tree.go. Hidden tests (not in the repo) named TestRouteParamsNotEmpty and TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePathWithMultipleChildrenAndWildcard must pass after the fixes. The repo's tree_test.go and routes_test.go contain similar tests that currently pass, so the deviations are subtle. Study tree.go thoroughly (getValue, addRoute, insertChild, addChild, incrementChildPrio, findCaseInsensitivePath, findCaseInsensitivePathRec, shiftNRuneBytes) and compare with the behaviour its comments describe and the existing tests require. Bug 1 (params not empty): write a TEMPORARY test /gin/zz_probe_tree_test.go (you MUST delete it when done) that builds a router with routes "/test/:param", "/test/:param/foo/:bar", "/test/:param/*action", "/test/*action" and asserts c.Params is non-empty with correct keys/values for requests /test/foo, /test/foo/foo/bar, /test/foo/bar/baz, /test/foo/bar; find why params come out empty and fix. Bug 2 (case-insensitive path with multiple children and a wildcard): in the same temporary test build a tree with routes like "/a/b", "/a/c", "/a/:p", "/a/:p/d", "/x/*all" and check findCaseInsensitivePath returns the case-corrected path for "/A/B", "/A/C", "/A/FOO", "/A/FOO/D", "/X/Y/Z"; fix the deviation. Make minimal edits; run `cd /gin && go test ./...` before and after and ensure no pre-existing test fails. NOTE: other agents edit other files concurrently; if a compile error comes from a zz_probe_*_test.go file that is not yours, wait 20s and retry; never modify files you did not create. Report exact diffs, before/after results, confirmation probe file deleted.

Go repo at /gin (gin-gonic/gin). TWO bugs were injected into /gin/context.go. Find the injected deviations and fix them minimally. Read /gin/response_writer.go and /gin/response_writer_test.go carefully and compare the code against its own comments, the ResponseWriter interface contract (Status() returns the HTTP response status code; WriteHeaderNow forces the header out) and the behaviour the existing tests rely on.
